Build the (i, j) triggering-pair index for re-estimation

Source: R/trigger_reestimate.R
trigger_pairs.Rd

Enumerates ordered event pairs (i, j) where j could plausibly have triggered i: j happened strictly before i, within window_days, and within window_dist in both spatial dimensions.

Usage

trigger_pairs(events, window_days = 90, window_dist = 1000)

Arguments

events

A semihawkes_events object (from prepare_events()).

window_days

Maximum number of days after j that i can occur; default 90 (matches the original script's actual filter, <= 90.0).

window_dist

Maximum absolute distance (in both x and y) between i and j, in the linear units of the working CRS (metres for a UTM projection); default 1000, i.e. 1 km, the same as the default reach of the spatial triggering kernel (see Choosing the triggering reach in fit_semihawkes()).

Value

A data frame with integer columns i, j (row indices into events$events), one row per qualifying pair.

Scalability

Once the events are sorted by day, the events that j could have triggered (those after it and within window_days) form one run, found with findInterval(); only those are checked against window_dist. Time and memory therefore grow with the number of candidate pairs rather than with n^2, as they did when every pair was compared. Pairs are returned in the same order as before: by j, then by i.

Examples

ev <- prepare_events(sim_events, sim_region, date_col = "date")
pairs <- trigger_pairs(ev, window_days = 30, window_dist = 1000)
nrow(pairs)
#> [1] 667
head(pairs)
#>   i j
#> 1 6 1
#> 2 8 1
#> 3 3 2
#> 4 4 2
#> 5 5 2
#> 6 7 2
